parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility ban, birth-sex custody/ward rule, or documented police targeting of visitors is shown; same-sex conduct is lawful and hate-crime law covers gender identity, with Pride, LGBT centres and official support indicating broad social acceptance. Against that, enforcement is documented as inconsistent, hate-crime investigations inadequate, judicial handling uneven and victims reluctant to report, so paper protections are only partially operative. Anti-gender disinformation and a disrupted Pride show hostility, while a prosecutor did charge a homophobic accommodation refusal, outcome unstated. Border/document treatment is unresolved—an open question, not a documented exposure. Resident-only matters (LGR, adoption, IVF, blood donation) are not counted as traveller protections or exposures. Overall: reduced but uneven protection, with no universal-exposure measure.
